item.title: Man Dies After Being Shot in the Quintas Quijote Neighborhood
item.description:
“Sol Prendido” for Borderland Beat 






The man, approximately 50 years old, was attacked at the intersection of Voltaria and Dornajo streets and taken by his family to a hospital, where he died while receiving medical care


A man, approximately 50 years old, died after being shot on the streets of the Quintas Quijote neighborhood; he sustained at least one gunshot wound to the head.


The incident took place at the intersection of Voltaria and Dornajo streets, where the man was found with a gunshot wound. Following the attack, his relatives acted quickly and decided to transport him to a hospital themselves.


The injured man was taken in a private vehicle to a hospital located on Periférico de la Juventud, where he was admitted to the emergency room for medical treatment. However, despite the medical team's efforts, he passed away while receiving care.


After the death was confirmed, Municipal and State Police officers deployed to the scene to document the incident and carry out the necessary procedures.


Authorities awaited the arrival of the agency responsible for conducting the investigation, processing the crime scene, and removing the body. So far, no further details have been released regarding those responsible for the attack or the possible motive.



The intersection of Voltaria and Dornajo streets in Chihuahua, Chihuahua. 



The Quintas Quijote neighborhood of Chihuahua, Chihuahua





Source: El Heraldo de Chihuahua

item.title: US Forces Down Around 100 Cartel Drones at Southern Border in August
item.description:
By "El Huaso" for Borderland Beat

Drones being use by warring Gulf Cartel factions in Tamaulipas, 2025.

The Pentagon disclosed that U.S. military units assigned to Joint Task Force–Southern Border took down approximately 100 suspected cartel drones along the U.S.-Mexico border in August 2026. This is the first time U.S. authorities have provided information on the number of cartel drones they have downed.

NewsNation separately reported that about 300 suspected cartel drones were downed in the first eight months of 2026. Operations were coordinated with Mexican military and border authorities. Pentagon spokesperson Kingsley Wilson said the systems are defensive, intended to protect U.S. personnel and border security missions from cartel drone threats. Officials did not name specific cartels or exact locations for the August incidents.

Mexican criminal groups primarily use drones near the U.S. border to surveil U.S. law enforcement and  transport small amounts of drugs. Drones have been used in combat in the state of Tamaulipas between criminal groups.

Sources: FoxNews, NewsNation, Borderland Beat Archives

item.title: Three Captured after CJNG Car Bomb in Ojocaliente, Zacatecas
item.description:
By “El Huaso” for Borderland Beat


Five days after a devastating CJNG car bomb attack at the Municipal Police station in Ojocaliente, Zacatecas which injured eleven and damaged dozens of buildings, Mexican authorities have provided additional information on the attack.



Last Sunday, August 30, around 7:50 p.m., a parked vehicle detonated right outside the Municipal Police station in Ojocaliente, a city 45 kilometers south east of the state capitol.The detonation injured eleven people, 2 police officers and 9 civilians, completely destroyed the police station, as well as damaging dozens of vehicles and residences in the city center. The bombing, the third using explosives against state forces in Zacatecas state in the last seven days, was part of a CJNG campaign against local authorities.


Today, Mexico’s Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch confirmed that three men have been arrested for the bombing, including Juan Pedro "N," who allegedly placed 200 kilograms of improvised explosive (IEDs) inside the car, who was arrested on August 31. Authorities also seized a fragmentation grenade, another IED, ammunition, tire spikes, drugs, a telephone and a vehicle.


Juan Pedro "N"

Later, authorities arrested two other men, Hipólito "N" and Miguel "N", who allegedly carried out surveillance prior to the attack.

Zacatecas authorities say the attack was retaliation by an organized crime group for the capture of one of its members on Saturday in the municipality of Villa García, near the border with Aguascalientes. The arrest followed an earlier remotely detonated explosive attack against a state police patrol on a highway in Villa García, in which a state police officer and a civilian were injured.

According to figures from the Zacatecas government, 17 incidents involving the use of explosive devices linked to the CJNG were recorded between 2024 and 2026. At least 10 explosive attacks have occurred in Zacatecas so far this year, including seven targeting security forces, according to El Universal. Security researcher David Saucedo wrote that the CJNG was behind this attack as well. The CJNG are currently fighting the "Mayiza" faction of the Sinaloa Cartel.


Sources: Borderland Beat, NTR Zacatecas, SinEmbargo, El Universal, El Universal

item.title: Mexican Security Forces Kill Luis Enrique Barragán Chávez, a.k.a. “R5” and “Wicho de los Reyes”
item.description:
In the early morning of August 31, the Mexican Army, with support from the Secretariat of Security and Citizen Protection, conducted a security operation in the Sierra of Michoacán that resulted in the death of Luis Enrique Barragán Chávez, a.k.a. “R5” and “Wicho de los Reyes.”

 

Who Was “R5”?

According to U.S. authorities, Luis Enrique Barragán Chávez was a regional leader and chief of hitmen (jefe de sicarios) for the Los Reyes Cartel. Barragán Chávez reportedly became involved in Michoacán's armed groups alongside his brother-in-law, with whom he initially fought Los Caballeros Templarios as part of the self-defense (autodefensas) movement. The two later formed their own criminal organization.

 

What Is the Los Reyes Cartel?

The Los Reyes Cartel is a Michoacán-based criminal organization that operates as a faction of Carteles Unidos, an alliance of several criminal groups active across the state.

 

Carteles Unidos and Michoacán

According to U.S. authorities, Carteles Unidos emerged as an alliance of smaller Michoacán-based cartels seeking to prevent larger criminal organizations from expanding into the state, particularly CJNG. The alliance has reportedly been engaged in a territorial conflict with CJNG since mid-August 2019.

“Carteles Unidos is a transnational criminal and drug trafficking organization that controls large areas of Michoacán. Acting as an umbrella organization, it unites several Michoacán-based cartels to acquire, manufacture, and distribute methamphetamine, fentanyl, and cocaine for smuggling into the United States.” The organization is also involved in extortion and other criminal activities.

Carteles Unidos has been linked to the recruitment of foreign mercenaries and the use of improvised explosive devices, including attacks that resulted in the deaths of Mexican soldiers. According to U.S. allegations, profits from drug sales in the United States were used to finance armed operations in Michoacán, acquire heavy weaponry, hire Colombian mercenaries, bribe local officials, and finance lavish lifestyles for cartel leaders.

According to U.S. authorities, Carteles Unidos has also been associated with extortion targeting avocado and lime producers, with those who refuse or are unable to make the demanded payments reportedly facing threats, disappearance, or death.

 

 What Was “R5” Accused Of?

In July 2023, U.S. prosecutors formally charged Luis Enrique Barragán Chávez in the District of Columbia with offenses related to conspiracies to traffic drugs and firearms. The allegations against R5 and Carteles Unidos involved drug trafficking, including the production and trafficking of synthetic opioids to the United States, as well as terrorism and extortion in Mexico's agricultural sector.

Barragán Chávez allegedly led armed factions of Carteles Unidos that enforced territorial control using assault weapons, improvised explosive devices, armed drones, armored vehicles, and foreign mercenaries.

 

What Was the Reward for “R5”?

On August 14, 2025, the U.S. government offered a reward of up to $3 million for information leading to Barragán Chávez's arrest and/or conviction.

 

International Connections

U.S. investigations have traced Carteles Unidos' criminal network from clandestine drug laboratories in Michoacán to major distribution hubs across the United States, with related cases pursued in the District of Columbia and the Eastern District of Tennessee. The investigations illustrate the international dimension of the organization, connecting drug production and armed operations in Michoacán with distribution networks operating across multiple U.S. states.

 

Sources:  treasury.gov - justice.gov - state.gov
